cautions: Candidate sets overlap both across concepts and across passes and are not additive.
Counts are records, not deduplicated unique problems.
Stored answer metadata does not establish curriculum or display approval.
Grade and published point tier are search hints, not calibrated learner difficulty.
Set A and Set B are complementary Level 1-2 courses, not difficulty levels 1 and 2.
Source-linked subskills describe curriculum evidence, not verified tags on each candidate question.
No private question text, answer, email identifiers, or asset is exported.

sourceCurricula.label: Think Academy MK 300, six 2024 workbooks
sourceCurricula.scope: Grades 1-2 and 3-4, each at 3/4/5-point tiers; 600 source occurrences, including 80 review-role occurrences.

sourceLessons.title: Fun With Patterns
sourceLessons.summary: Repeating pictures, colors, events, and addition/subtraction rules.

sourceLessons.title: Picture It, Solve It!
sourceLessons.summary: Use simple pictures to track quantities, positions, intervals, and changing states.

sourceLessons.title: Let's Work Backwards
sourceLessons.summary: Start from a known end state; reverse the order and direction of operations.

sourceLessons.title: Tick-Tock Time Travelers
sourceLessons.summary: Read clocks/calendars, convert familiar time units, and reason about elapsed time.

sourceLessons.title: Puzzle Mania
sourceLessons.summary: Infer missing pieces, compare outlines, and reconstruct a pictured whole.

sourceLessons.title: Flat Figures and Shapes
sourceLessons.summary: Distinguish flat/solid objects; compare and cut shapes; count missing units and compare coverage.

sourceLessons.title: Think, Guess, Check!
sourceLessons.summary: Use parity, digit clues, and equal-sum constraints to try and revise candidates.

sourceLessons.title: Money, Money, Money
sourceLessons.summary: List prices, combine costs, find change, repeat equal prices, and compare purchases.

sourceLessons.title: Symmetry Quest
sourceLessons.summary: Distinguish identical figures from mirror images; use axes, folds, stamps, and successive flips.

sourceLessons.title: Game On! / MK 2012
sourceLessons.summary: Mixed synthesis: understand, choose a strategy, carry it out, check the result.

sourceLessons.title: Math in Motion: Paths and Mazes
sourceLessons.summary: Trace legal routes, backtrack from dead ends, minimize crossings, and count possible routes.

sourceLessons.title: Compare, Get in Line!
sourceLessons.summary: Use comparison clues, order values or objects, and reason about positions in a line.

sourceLessons.title: Spatial Secrets
sourceLessons.evidenceLocator: class notes slide 7 and worked examples
sourceLessons.summary: Track views, stacking order, overlaps, woven strips, and shape completion.

sourceLessons.title: Measure Up!
sourceLessons.evidenceLocator: class notes slide 5 and worked examples
sourceLessons.summary: Count equal units and compare lengths, heights, and route distances.

sourceLessons.title: Story Problems
sourceLessons.evidenceLocator: class notes slides 4-10; instructor lesson summary
sourceLessons.summary: Use organized lists and tables for routes, repeated processes, pairings, and allocations.

sourceLessons.title: How Old Are You?
sourceLessons.summary: Ages change together; differences stay fixed; a sum grows once per person each year.

sourceLessons.title: Solids in Action
sourceLessons.evidenceLocator: class notes slides 7-9 and worked examples
sourceLessons.summary: Identify solids, faces, edges, and vertices; infer hidden cubes and match views/nets.

sourceLessons.title: Balance the Scales / Balancing Act
sourceLessons.evidenceLocator: class notes slide 7 and worked examples
sourceLessons.summary: Preserve equality on both sides, substitute equivalent groups, and chain exchanges.

sourceLessons.title: Logical Reasoning / Got Logic?
sourceLessons.evidenceLocator: class notes slide 7 and worked examples
sourceLessons.summary: Combine explicit and implied clues; revise an arrangement while satisfying every condition.

sourceLessons.title: The 4-Step Method and MK 2022
sourceLessons.summary: Mixed synthesis with pattern, diagram, list, table, visualization, trial, and equation strategies.

concepts.label: Counting
objectivesByPass: Count visible objects once; choose the relevant objects; count missing units.
Organize groups, overlapping regions, and inclusive endpoints without double counting.
Count by cases and complements; derive rather than enumerate a larger total.
Prove a counting strategy; use invariants and combinatorial structure.

concepts.label: Symmetry
objectivesByPass: Match mirror halves and complete one reflection across a visible line.
Track folds and reflections across different axes; distinguish turns from mirrors.
Combine transformations and reason about invariant features.
Use symmetry to reduce cases and justify geometric relationships.

concepts.label: Addition & Subtraction
objectivesByPass: Join, remove, and compare small visible quantities.
Use inverse operations and two-step comparison stories.
Choose an efficient decomposition and reason with signed quantities.
Reason about expressions and additive invariants without brute-force calculation.

concepts.label: Patterns
objectivesByPass: Identify a repeating unit or one-step growing pattern.
Find missing positions and use the period of a cycle.
Compare recursive and position-based rules.
Generalize a sequence and justify an indexed or recursive rule.

concepts.label: Shape Building
objectivesByPass: Recognize boundaries and fit or combine simple pieces.
Decompose and tile shapes while preserving their boundaries.
Use angles, congruence, and tiling constraints to organize a construction.
Use similarity, decomposition, and auxiliary shapes after ratios and scale have been taught.

concepts.label: Logic
objectivesByPass: Combine two concrete clues to eliminate an impossible arrangement.
Order or place several objects; work backward through a short process.
Track interacting constraints and exhaust a small set of cases.
Use contradiction, invariants, and complete case analysis.

concepts.label: Groups & Sharing
objectivesByPass: Make equal groups and share concrete objects fairly.
Link multiplication and division, including a meaningful remainder.
Compare ratios and unit rates in multi-step situations.
Reason proportionally with changing rates and constraints.

concepts.label: Number & Digits
objectivesByPass: Read place value and compose or compare numbers from digits.
Use parity, place-value constraints, and simple divisibility.
Use factors, multiples, remainders, and digit constraints together.
Apply modular, factorization, and exponent structure.

concepts.label: Routes & Grids
objectivesByPass: Follow a path, read positions, and distinguish steps from visited points.
Compare routes on grids and obey one-way or no-repeat rules.
Count constrained routes and use connectivity.
Combine coordinate and graph structure to prove a route property.

concepts.label: Fractions
objectivesByPass: Recognize equal parts and halves in concrete pictures.
Compare and compose fractions; reconstruct a whole from a part.
Connect fraction operations, decimals, and percentages.
Reason with successive fractional changes and constrained proportions.

concepts.label: Solids & Views
objectivesByPass: Match a simple solid to a view and count visible blocks.
Infer hidden blocks and match nets or multiple views.
Reason about sections, painted faces, and surface versus volume.
Use a spatial decomposition to justify a three-dimensional relationship.

concepts.label: Length & Measure
objectivesByPass: Compare lengths and measure with repeated equal units.
Combine measurements, choose units, and interpret a simple scale.
Convert units and relate scale, capacity, and distance.
Model an indirect measurement and justify the chosen units and scale.

concepts.label: Money & Value
objectivesByPass: Combine coin values and make a small purchase.
Make change and compare equivalent purchases.
Reason through exchanges, bundles, and proportional prices.
Optimize a purchase or exchange with multiple constraints.

concepts.label: Time
objectivesByPass: Read a clock or calendar and order short time intervals.
Find elapsed time across hour and day boundaries.
Coordinate schedules, periodic events, and travel time.
Reason about simultaneous cycles and rate-time constraints.

concepts.label: Area & Boundary
objectivesByPass: Compare covered space using whole squares and trace a boundary.
Distinguish area from perimeter and decompose a rectilinear region.
Find composite or shaded area using equalities and subtraction.
Prove area relations and optimize a boundary under constraints.

concepts.label: Missing Values
objectivesByPass: Find one missing amount in a pictured balance or equality.
Link two equalities and solve a simple symbol code.
Translate relations into equations and solve coupled unknowns.
Reason about functions, systems, and algebraic structure.

concepts.label: Possibilities
objectivesByPass: Reserve: small concrete choice lists, if a separate world is worthwhile.
List combinations systematically without missing or repeating an outcome.
Use product structure, organized cases, and complementary counts.
Use combinations, permutations, and inclusion-exclusion with justification.

concepts.label: Chance & Data
objectivesByPass: Reserve: read a simple picture chart; no early probability prerequisite.
Read a data display and identify all equally likely outcomes.
Compare probabilities and aggregate or interpret data.
Reason about conditional information and structured sample spaces.

countingOneProposedQuestions.rationale: Count animals; exclude non-animals and include the joey.
Count only stars with five points.
Track whole bicycles through overlap; crop out the next question.
Count matches systematically by roof, rows, and columns.
Count spots in visible groups without counting the ladybugs.
Count whole ropes rather than exposed segments; endpoints provide a strategy.
Count only circles containing the kangaroo.
Count every touched grid cell once, using a row-by-row scan.
Reconstruct a five-by-five grid to count missing squares.
Count missing brick units across staggered rows.
Stretch: distinguish cuts from resulting rope pieces.
